blocks.text: REP:000–022 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Repair entity block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 100 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 18 dedicated Repair entity-layer soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: REP:0xx names substrate-neutral restoration-condition entities. The inward triplet identifies one acceptable condition internal to a reference entity; the outward triplet identifies the acceptable restoration condition of one distinct target; and the systemic triplet identifies one correlated acceptable condition across multiple participants. The third trit changes only persistent identity, present realization, or dormancy.

REP:000 — persistent internal restoration condition — An acceptable condition internal to one reference entity that remains identified as that entity's restoration standard independently of whether it is presently realized.
REP:001 — manifest internal restoration condition — An acceptable condition internal to one reference entity that is presently realized as that entity's restored state.
REP:002 — dormant internal restoration condition — An acceptable condition internal to one reference entity that remains identified as its restoration standard without being presently realized.

REP:010 — persistent target restoration condition — An acceptable condition of one distinct reference target that remains identified as that target's restoration standard independently of whether it is presently realized.
REP:011 — manifest target restoration condition — An acceptable condition of one distinct reference target that is presently realized as that target's restored state.
REP:012 — dormant target restoration condition — An acceptable condition of one distinct reference target that remains identified as its restoration standard without being presently realized.

REP:020 — persistent shared restoration condition — One correlated acceptable condition that remains identified across multiple participant entities within a shared system as their restoration standard independently of its present realization pattern.
REP:021 — manifest shared restoration condition — One correlated acceptable condition that is presently realized across multiple participant entities within a shared system as their restored state.

REP:022 — dormant shared restoration condition — One correlated acceptable condition that remains identified across multiple participant entities within a shared system as their restoration standard without being presently realized.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode domain-specific health, integrity, validity, correctness, cleanliness, availability, or absence of fault; baseline records, checkpoints, backups, acceptance rules, beliefs, or evidence; actual healing, repair, recalibration, recovery, maintenance, replacement, or reconstruction; recoverability, repairability, restorative resources, schedules, future realization, cause, or guaranteed success. A persistent root may co-occur with its manifest or dormant sibling; manifest and dormant are mutually exclusive for the same condition at one reference time. Lexical dormancy remains distinct from runtime [2]/num uncertainty.
